assumptions: Fighter (installed pufferlib ocean chess) is the baseline for feature comparison
Fighter has a much simpler architecture: 72 obs, 4096 actions, no FEN, no reward shaping, no random bot, no human play, no render, no PGN, no debug hooks
Our env already has FEN curriculum (fen_file + fen_curric_pct), reward shaping, SEE, threefold repetition, and many more features than fighter
The new architecture (per other agent plans) may change to 1-agent-per-env, which affects how some ops features are wired
human_play, render, PGN, and random_bot are purely additive features that do not disrupt existing training
starting_fen (single fixed FEN for all games) is distinct from fen_curric_pct (random FEN from file with probability)

changes.title: Add starting_fen config parameter
changes.description: Add a 'starting_fen' string kwarg that, when set, initializes ALL games from that FEN on every reset (instead of standard starting position). Unlike fen_curric_pct (probabilistic, from a file), starting_fen is deterministic and always applies. Useful for debugging specific positions and targeted training. In C: store a char[256] starting_fen in ChessEnv or VecEnv; in c_reset, if starting_fen[0] != 0, call setup_from_fen() instead of setup_initial_board(). In binding.c: parse 'starting_fen' string kwarg in vec_init. In chess_env.py: accept starting_fen param, pass to binding. In config: add starting_fen = '' (empty = standard start).
changes.gap_analysis: Fighter has NO FEN support at all. Our env has fen_curric_pct + fen_file but lacks a simple 'always start from this FEN' option. starting_fen is complementary.
acceptance: starting_fen='' => standard starting position (no change)
starting_fen='rnbqkbnr/pppppppp/8/8/4P3/8/PPPP1PPP/RNBQKBNR b KQkq e3 0 1' => all games start from 1.e4
starting_fen interacts correctly with fen_curric_pct: if both set, fen_curric_pct overrides with probability p, else starting_fen is used
CLI: --env.starting-fen 'FEN_STRING' works

changes.title: Add random_bot opponent mode
changes.description: Add a 'random_bot_pct' float kwarg (0.0-1.0). With probability random_bot_pct, one side (Black by default, or configurable via 'random_bot_color') plays uniformly random legal moves instead of using the policy. Implementation: in c_step, after reading the current player's action, if that player is the random bot, ignore their action and pick a random legal move (already have chess_rand_int + generate_legal_moves). In VecEnv, store random_bot_pct and per-game random_bot_active flag set on reset. In 1-agent topology (where only one side is the learner), the random bot would be the non-learner side. Useful for curriculum: start training against random, gradually reduce random_bot_pct.
changes.gap_analysis: Fighter has NO random bot support. Our env also lacks it. This is a key curriculum feature for early training.
acceptance: random_bot_pct=0.0 => pure self-play (no change)
random_bot_pct=1.0 => one side always plays random legal moves
random_bot_pct=0.5 => 50% of games have a random bot opponent
Random bot always picks uniformly from legal moves
Per-game flag is set at reset time (not per-step)
CLI: --env.random-bot-pct 0.5 works
Log field: 'random_bot_games' tracks fraction of games with random bot

changes.title: Add ASCII board render function in C
changes.description: Add a C function board_to_ascii(ChessEnv* env, char* buf, int bufsize) that writes an ASCII representation of the board to buf (8 lines of 8 chars with file/rank labels, piece chars: KQRBNPkqrbnp, '.' for empty). Add a Python-callable vec_render(handle, game_index) that returns the ASCII string. In chess_env.py, implement render() to call vec_render for game 0 and print to stdout. Also add render_mode='ansi' support returning the string.
changes.gap_analysis: Fighter has render() as a no-op (pass). Our env also has render() as no-op. Basic ASCII rendering is essential for debugging and human play.
acceptance: render() prints an 8x8 ASCII board with piece symbols
render_mode='ansi' returns the string without printing
Board is shown from White's perspective with file (a-h) and rank (1-8) labels
Current player indicator: 'White to move' or 'Black to move'
Move number and halfmove clock shown

changes.title: Add PGN export / move history tracking
changes.description: Track move history per game for PGN export. In ChessEnv, add int move_history[512] (encoded as from*64+to) and int move_history_count. In apply_move_ex, record each move. Add a C function game_to_pgn(ChessEnv* env, char* buf, int bufsize) that converts the move history to standard algebraic notation (SAN) PGN. Add a Python-callable vec_get_pgn(handle, game_index) returning the PGN string. Add a vec_save_pgns(handle, filepath) that dumps all completed game PGNs to a file. Useful for post-training analysis and debugging.
changes.gap_analysis: Neither fighter nor our env tracks move history or exports PGN. This is critical for understanding what the agent actually learns.
acceptance: Move history is recorded in C for each game
PGN output includes standard headers: Event, White, Black, Result
Moves are in standard algebraic notation (e.g., 'e4', 'Nf3', 'O-O')
vec_get_pgn(handle, 0) returns valid PGN string
PGN can be loaded in standard chess tools (lichess, chess.com analysis)
Move history resets on game reset
Optional: save PGN every N episodes to a file via callback

changes.title: Add human_play interactive mode
changes.description: Add a human_play() function (or human_play.py script) that runs a single game between a human and the trained policy. Terminal-based: render board as ASCII, prompt human for moves in UCI notation (e.g., 'e2e4'), validate, step the env. Load a checkpoint, create a single-game env, alternate between human input and policy inference. Requires: render (OPS-03), a way to load a checkpoint and run inference. The human can choose to play White or Black. Ctrl+C to quit. Optionally show policy's move probabilities.
changes.gap_analysis: Neither fighter nor our env has human play. Essential for qualitative evaluation.
acceptance: python human_play.py --checkpoint path/to/model.pt --color white
ASCII board rendered after each move
Human enters moves in UCI format: 'e2e4' (from_sq to_sq)
Invalid moves are rejected with a message, user re-prompted
Game ends naturally (checkmate/stalemate/draw) with result shown
Policy inference uses the loaded checkpoint
Works with both Policy and ChessLSTM models

changes.title: Add seed reproducibility and state dump
changes.description: Ensure full deterministic replay given a seed. Add vec_get_state(handle, game_index) -> dict with all game state (board, castling, ep, halfmove, fullmove, current_player, step_count, rng_state, move_history). Add vec_set_state(handle, game_index, state_dict) to restore. Useful for debugging specific sequences. Also add a vec_get_rng_state(handle, game_index) and vec_set_rng_state for reproducibility testing.
changes.gap_analysis: Fighter has seed in vec_reset but no state dump/restore. Our env has seed in vec_reset and rng_state per game. Missing: Python-accessible state dump for debugging.
acceptance: vec_get_state returns a dict with complete game state
vec_set_state restores a game to exact prior state
Two runs with the same seed produce identical game sequences
State can be serialized to JSON for logging

changes.title: Add comprehensive CLI/config flags documentation and missing flags
changes.description: Ensure all env parameters are exposed in config/chess.ini and documented. Current missing flags to add: (1) starting_fen (from OPS-01), (2) random_bot_pct (from OPS-02), (3) random_bot_color (default 'black'), (4) render_interval (how often to render during training, 0=never), (5) pgn_save_interval (save PGN every N episodes, 0=never), (6) pgn_save_path (directory for PGN files). Also add comments in the .ini file explaining each parameter.
changes.gap_analysis: Fighter config has only: num_envs, max_steps, illegal_move_penalty, report_interval. Our config already has all reward shaping params + FEN curriculum. Need to add the new ops features.
acceptance: Every env kwarg appears in chess.ini with a default value
Comments in .ini explain each parameter
CLI override works: --env.random-bot-pct 0.5
New parameters have sensible defaults that don't change existing behavior

changes.title: Add FEN board-to-string utility for logging
changes.description: Add a C function board_to_fen(ChessEnv* env, char* buf, int bufsize) that exports the current board state as a FEN string. Add a Python-callable vec_get_fen(handle, game_index) returning the FEN string. Useful for: logging interesting positions, creating FEN curriculum files from training runs, debugging.
changes.gap_analysis: Our env has setup_from_fen (FEN parser) but no board_to_fen (FEN writer). Fighter has neither. Symmetric FEN read/write is useful.
acceptance: board_to_fen produces valid FEN strings
Round-trip: setup_from_fen(board_to_fen(env)) == identity
vec_get_fen(handle, 0) returns FEN string from Python
FEN includes all 6 fields (pieces, side, castling, ep, halfmove, fullmove)

changes.title: Add training callback hooks for periodic PGN/FEN logging
changes.description: Add optional callback support in the env's step() method or as a separate training hook: (1) Every pgn_save_interval episodes, save the last N completed game PGNs to pgn_save_path. (2) Every fen_log_interval steps, log the current board FEN for a sample of games. (3) Optional: save 'interesting' games (decisive games with few moves, long games, etc.) separately. This requires OPS-04 (PGN) and OPS-08 (FEN export).
changes.gap_analysis: Neither fighter nor our env has any training-time debug artifact generation.
acceptance: PGN files appear in pgn_save_path at the configured interval
FEN logging writes to a configurable log file or stdout
Callbacks don't measurably impact training throughput (<1% SPS loss)
Disabled by default (pgn_save_interval=0, fen_log_interval=0)

changes.title: Add dynamic FEN curriculum adjustment API
changes.description: We already have vec_load_fens and vec_set_fen_pct in our binding.c. Expose these in chess_env.py as methods: env.load_fens(path) and env.set_fen_pct(pct). This allows training scripts to dynamically adjust FEN curriculum during training (e.g., start at fen_curric_pct=0.5, gradually reduce to 0.0). Also add a method to get current fen_count and fen_curric_pct.
changes.gap_analysis: The C API exists (vec_load_fens, vec_set_fen_pct) but chess_env.py doesn't expose them. Fighter has none of this.
acceptance: env.load_fens('/path/to/new_fens.txt') loads new FEN file and returns count
env.set_fen_pct(0.3) updates curriculum percentage at runtime
env.fen_count and env.fen_pct properties return current values
Dynamic adjustment doesn't require env recreation

feature_gap_fighter_vs_ours.fighter_has_we_dont: Nothing. Fighter is strictly a subset. Fighter has: 72 obs, 4096 flat actions, no FEN, no reward shaping, no threefold repetition, no action masking, no move caching, no SEE, hardcoded -0.001 step penalty, random move on illegal action.
feature_gap_fighter_vs_ours.we_have_fighter_doesnt: FEN curriculum (fen_file + fen_curric_pct), 20+ reward shaping params, SEE hanging detection, threefold repetition, action masking in obs, two-phase actions (97), legal move caching, int32/int64 action dtype support, dynamic FEN loading API, comprehensive logging (material_score, positional_score, chess_moves, repetitions, etc.)
feature_gap_fighter_vs_ours.neither_has: random_bot, human_play, render, PGN export, board_to_fen, state dump/restore, starting_fen, training callbacks

priority_order: OPS-03: ASCII render (medium - needed by OPS-05)
OPS-04: PGN export (medium - needed by OPS-05, OPS-09)
OPS-10: dynamic FEN API exposure (medium - API exists, just expose)
OPS-09: training callbacks (low - depends on OPS-04, OPS-08)
